(E) The full loop with the box (γ = 10⁻², τ = 10⁻⁴, 12 seeds, 10⁶ slow units; P_B's vertices (0.558, 0.206, 0.236), (0.295, 0.470, 0.236), (0.295, 0.206, 0.499)): each run is the unboxed one record for record until a coordinate first leaves B (without the correction from 1.7·10⁴ to 4.1·10⁵ slow units; at κ_F = 2 from 2.4·10⁴ on, one seed never); without the correction the masses' spread at 10⁶ is 0.049, 0.075, 0.057 against 0.145, 0.154, 0.081 without the box, each seed's masses still 0.10–0.18 from the nearest vertex — on their way, at the entropic drift's slow rate; at κ_F = 2 the masses' mean at 10⁶ (0.3803 ± 0.0093, 0.2961 ± 0.0122, 0.3236 ± 0.0102) is within 0.41 standard errors of W♯, every seed within 0.010–0.080 of it; |α| ≤ 5.03, the fit error 0.026. (F) In Proposition D‴.37's runs without a leak (H) every record with |α_k| > 10 but one (3860 of 3861, on 8, 3 and 7 of the 12 seeds) has W_k within 0.01 of the saturation, and the exact fit's error (0.024): the gauge's channel; with the masses held near 1/3 by
the leak and no correction (Proposition D‴.38 (F)) every such record has W_k more than 0.05 above it and the fit error 0.041–0.043 (516 and 13 records, on 2 and 1 of the 16 seeds): the positions' own channel, the escape of (ii).


**Proposition D‴.40 (the gauge under general noise: the replicator's averaged fitness is the generator's image of one coordinate; at
leading order only each amplitude's own noise intensity drives its class's mass).** In the setting of Proposition D‴.36 (one particle per
class, the classes beyond the cohesion's range, the replicator at rate γ) let the positions carry a white noise of any constant
covariance Σ (per unit slow time) instead of 2τ diag(G), and write τ_k := Σ_{α_kα_k}/(2G_α) for the noise intensity on the k-th amplitude,
g_k := a_k/(β_k a′_k) and ψ_k := ∫g_k dα_k/G_α = (a_max²/(4β_kG_α))cosh(2α_k/a_max).

(i) *(the generator identity)* At fixed masses, in any stationary law of the positions — none exists under the cohesion leak alone
(Proposition D‴.39(i)); with the box V of Proposition D‴.39(iii) one does —,

    E[u_k] = −τ_k E[g′_k(α_k)] + E[g_k∂_{α_k}(J_coh + V)],   g′_k = (1 + (a_k/a_max)²)/(β_k a′_k),

exactly for the diffusion (for the Euler scheme up to its O(Δt) bias, E[Lψ_k]): the forces the gauge identity does not cover — the
cohesion's, zero between classes beyond its range, and the box's, zero inside B — are the only correction to −τ_kE[g′_k]. In the exact
fit's well, before the positions' first exit from it (times short against e^{ΔJ/τ}, Proposition D‴.39(ii)), the box's term is absent and
E[u_k] = −τ_kE[g′_k] up to exit terms. At leading order in the noise ū_k = −τ_kg′_k at the fit = −(τ_k/m)(1 + (a_k/a_max)²)/(W_ka′_k)
= −∂_{β_k}F_τ, F_τ(W) := Σ_kτ_k log(W_k − W_min,k²/W_k): at this order only each amplitude's own intensity enters, the noise's
correlations and its parts on the centres and widths do not; the O(τ²) terms — E[g′_k] over the fluctuations — depend on all of Σ. In the
slow-replicator limit the masses follow the replicator flow of ū, at leading order the Shahshahani gradient flow descending F_τ, whatever
Σ; Proposition D‴.37(ii) is the case τ_k = τ.

(ii) *(the nonlinear coordinates)* If the noise does not reach the amplitudes (Σ_{α_k·} = 0 for every k), the masses' diffusion D of
Katzenberger's limit vanishes identically at every γ, and E[u_k] = E[g_k∂_{α_k}(J_coh + V)]: zero in the well and at every order there,
so in the slow-replicator limit the gauge is frozen — it neither diffuses nor drifts —, while in the boxed stationary law the box's term
remains where the law reaches the wall. Dithering the centres and widths only keeps the exploration of the positions and removes the
noise's selection of the masses; a log-barrier on the masses (Proposition D‴.38's masses form, any τ_B > 0) then drives them to W♯
deterministically, at the rate κ_Fγτ_B.

(iii) *(the correction for any noise)* The masses form with the classes' own levels, c_k = κ_F(τ_k/m)(1 + Ŵ_k²/W_k²)/(W_k − Ŵ_k²/W_k),
cancels the drift at leading order at κ_F = 1 and for κ_F > 1 drives the masses to the maximiser W♯_τ of F_τ (the representable masses'
analytic centre for the weights τ_k; W♯ for equal levels); the plug-in form at the levels τ_k is τ_kg′_k(α_k), so its average cancels the
noise's part −τ_kE[g′_k] of (i) — not the box's or the cohesion's — in the slow-replicator limit, where the denominator's floor is
inactive. τ_k is the quadratic-variation rate of α_k's noise over 2G_α: read from the increments Δα_k the drift's part biases it by
Δt·E[b_k²]/(2G_ατ_k), O(Δt); the loop, which knows its drift b_k, reads the noise increments Δα_k − Δt·b_k instead.

*Proof.* The gauge identity: f̂ depends on (β_k, α_k) only through β_k a(α_k), and the cohesion energy is constant between classes beyond
its range, so ∂_{β_k}J_fit = g_k ∂_{α_k}J_fit and u_k = −∂_{β_k}J_fit = −g_k ∂_{α_k}J_fit, at every state. The positions' generator at fixed
masses is Lψ = −(G∇(J_fit + J_coh + V))·∇ψ + ½tr(Σ∇²ψ); for ψ_k, ψ′_k = g_k/G_α and ψ″_k = g′_k/G_α, so Lψ_k = −g_k∂_{α_k}(J_fit + J_coh + V) +
τ_kg′_k = u_k − g_k∂_{α_k}(J_coh + V) + τ_kg′_k. With the box the stationary law has Gaussian tails beyond B (V is quadratic there), ψ_k
grows like e^{2|α_k|/a_max} and is integrable against it, and stationarity, E[Lψ_k] = 0 (Itô's formula on the stationary process), is
(i). For the Euler chain E[ψ_k(α_{n+1}) − ψ_k(α_n)] = 0 exactly, and the conditional expectation of a cosh of a Gaussian increment is in
closed form: E[Lψ_k] = −E[b_k], b_k the per-step bias, O(Δt). In the well, before the exit, V's term is identically zero on the
trajectory. With a = a_max tanh(α/a_max), a′ = 1 − (a/a_max)²: g′ = (1/β)(a′(1 − a²/a_max²) + 2a²a′/a_max²)/(1 − a²/a_max²)² =
(1 + a²/a_max²)/(βa′); at the exact fit (a_k = A_k/W_k) this is m⁻¹ d/dW_k of log(W_k − W_min,k²/W_k), so the leading order is the stated
gradient; the fluctuations' correction is ½E[g‴_k]C_{α_kα_k} + g″_kμ_{α_k} with the positions' covariance C and mean shift μ, which depend on
all of Σ. The slow-replicator limit is the averaging principle of Proposition D‴.37(ii) with the positions' stationary law in place of
the Gibbs law. (ii) D = ∂W·PΣPᵀ·∂Wᵀ: the left null vectors of the linearisation of a gradient flow in the metric g are g times the
tangent vectors; the gauge's tangent lies in the amplitude–mass coordinates and the metric has no block coupling them to the centres and
widths, so P annihilates the centre and width directions at every γ; E[u_k] is (i) with τ_k = 0. (iii) The masses form at the levels τ_k
is −ū_k at the fit (κ_F = 1); for κ_F > 1 the masses ascend (κ_F − 1)F_τ, strictly concave (each term is D‴.38(ii)'s); the plug-in form
is τ_kg′_k(α_k) by the computation of g′; the quadratic variation of α_k's noise is Σ_{α_kα_k} per unit time, and Δα_k² = (Δtb_k + Δν_k)²
adds Δt²b_k² per step. ∎

*Status.* (i) proved for the boxed stationary law (the identity with the box's and the cohesion's terms; exact for the diffusion, for the
Euler chain up to its measured O(Δt) bias), the box-free form in the well up to exit terms (not quantified), the leading order and its
reading as the Shahshahani gradient of F_τ proved; (ii) D = 0 proved at every γ, the zero drift in the well, the box's term in the
stationary law numerical; (iii) proved at leading order (the masses form) and for the noise's part in the slow limit (the plug-in form).
Classical: the stationary adjoint (Stein) identity E[Lψ] = 0 for a test function of one coordinate — the configurational temperature
(Rugh; Jepps–Ayton–Evans) and generalised equipartition —; in equilibrium the mean force on a constrained coordinate with its Jacobian
term (the blue-moon ensemble, thermodynamic integration: Carter–Ciccotti–Hynes–Kapral; Sprik–Ciccotti; den Otter). New: the gauge
identity, which makes the replicator's fitness the generator's image of a function of one amplitude, so that its average under any
noise covariance is that amplitude's own level times E[g′_k] plus the forces the gauge does not cover; the freezing of the gauge when the
amplitudes are not dithered; the class-level correction with a level the loop reads from its own trajectory.

*Numerics* (`exp_gauge_noise.py` → `results/chaos/gauge_noise.md`; Proposition D‴.36's instance, τ = 10⁻⁴). (A) The trace formula (the
Gaussian expansion ū = ∇u·μ + ½tr(∇²u C) about the fit) against the closed form ū_k = −(τ_k/m)(1 + (a_k/a_max)²)/(W_ka′_k), at three points
of M, for isotropic noise, noise on the amplitudes only, per-class amplitude levels (2, 1, 1/2)τ, three random correlated covariances (τ_k/τ
from 1.46 to 5.77) and Part E's correlated noise: their replicator flows agree to 1.3·10⁻⁸–1.0·10⁻⁶; for the centres and widths only the
fitness is below 5.3·10⁻¹¹, the closed form zero. (B) Katzenberger's limit drift at γ = 10⁻⁵ against the replicator flow of the closed form:
within 1.1·10⁻⁴–8.8·10⁻⁴ for every noise with amplitude components; for the centres and widths only the drift is 8·10⁻¹⁶ per unit slow time
and the diffusion 10⁻³⁶ (against 10⁻¹³ for isotropic noise). (C) The centres and widths dithered only at finite γ: the drift per γτ is at
most 3.2·10⁻⁴, 7.2·10⁻⁵, 7.9·10⁻⁶, 8.0·10⁻⁷ at γ = 10⁻², …, 10⁻⁵ (O(γ); isotropic noise 0.03–0.93) and the diffusion per γ²τ below 1.1·10⁻²²
(isotropic 1.6–13): the gauge frozen. (D) The identity in simulation, at fixed masses 1/3 inside Proposition D‴.39's box (2·10⁵ slow units;
errors from 10 batch means), for isotropic, amplitudes-only and correlated noise at τ = 10⁻³ and 10⁻² and for the centres and widths alone
at 10⁻² — where the small-noise expansion does not apply: (i)'s box-free form E[u_k + τ_kg′_k] = 0 fails by up to 58 standard errors, its
residual the box's term E[g_k∂_{α_k}V] (3.9·10⁻² against 3.7·10⁻² ± 0.3·10⁻² at the largest; the cohesion's term below 10⁻⁷); the whole
identity, with the Euler chain's bias b_k computed per step in closed form (0.2–1.9% of τ_kE[g′_k]), holds: E[Lψ_k] + E[b_k] against the
martingale's error gives χ² = 24.8 for the 18 values with amplitude noise (the largest |z| 1.71) — they are not 18 independent draws: the
runs share one seed, and the four with diagonal noise draw the amplitudes' noise from the same three streams, so that their twelve values
(all positive) repeat three draws —, and by construction it is the boundary term (ψ_k(end) − ψ_k(start))/T, below 0.03 errors here, less the
martingale's mean; for the centres and widths alone, where the amplitudes see no noise, E[Lψ_k] + E[b_k] is the boundary term to 7·10⁻¹⁹.
The amplitudes' noise intensity read from their quadratic variation, τ̂_k, is within 1.4% of τ_k (0.25% without the drift's part). (E) The
full loop inside the box (γ = 0.01, τ = 10⁻⁴, 12 seeds, 10⁶ slow units): with the centres and widths dithered only the masses stay at their
start 1/3 (the second half's mean within 2·10⁻⁴ of it, the seeds' spread 3–10·10⁻⁴); adding the log-barrier at κ_F = 1 drives them to W♯ =
(0.3765, 0.2988, 0.3247) — 0.3758, 0.2995, 0.3247, within 8·10⁻⁴ —; under the correlated noise with the amplitude levels (2, 1, 1/2)τ and no
correction the masses drift (0.326, 0.246, 0.428 over the second half, 0.10 from W♯, the seeds' spread 0.03–0.04), and with the masses form
at the classes' levels (κ_F = 2) they move toward the weighted analytic centre W♯_τ = (0.4609, 0.2824, 0.2567): 0.409, 0.428, 0.440 for the
first mass at 10⁵, 3·10⁵, 10⁶ slow units, the second half's mean 0.022 from W♯_τ and 0.062 from W♯.

**Proposition D‴.41 (measurement noise on the gauge: no selection in continuous time; per update, the increment's second moment
selects).** In the setting of Proposition D‴.36 (one particle per class, the classes beyond the cohesion's range, the replicator at rate γ,
the manifold M of exact fits), let the loop be driven by the measured error: the residual r replaced by r + ξ in both laws — with the
desired regressor of Corollary D‴.33 the measurement noise enters through the error alone —, ξ a noise on the orbit's quadrature nodes, of
intensity v (⟨ξh⟩_ρ has the variance v⟨h²⟩_ρ per unit slow time), and no dither. Unless said otherwise ξ is homoscedastic and independent
over the nodes — the image of a measurement noise white on the orbit's resolution (correlation time τ_n ≪ T/N). In the coordinates
z = (Θ, log β) the loop is dz = ⟨(r + ξ)U⟩_ρ ds with

    U_x := mM∇_z f̂(x) = (β_iG∇_ϑΦ̃(x; ϑ_i),  γ(Φ̃(x; ϑ_i) − f̂(x)))_i,

M the flow's mobility (G on the positions, γ/β on log β, projected on Σβ = m): the noise enters along the descent's own vector fields. Write
F = ⟨rU⟩_ρ for the noiseless flow, Φ for its limit map, A = ∂F at a point of M (eigenvalues 0 on TM and −λ_i < 0), ψ_x := ∂Φ·U_x, and
Φ̃_k = a_kΦ_k (Φ_k the k-th bump's shape, a_k = a_max tanh(α_k/a_max) its amplitude).

(i) *(no diffusion along M)* On M every U_x is orthogonal to M in the flow's metric g = M⁻¹ — ⟨U_x, t⟩_g = m∂_t f̂(x) = 0 for t tangent to
M —, so the masses do not diffuse along M at order v (under dither they do, Proposition D‴.36).

(ii) *(no drift in continuous time)* For white noise in Stratonovich's sense — the limit of noise with smooth paths (Wong–Zakai) —, and for
a stationary noise with smooth paths and any correlation function in time, the drift along M vanishes at order v: Katzenberger's Itô
drift ½∂²Φ[Σ], Σ = v⟨UUᵀ⟩_ρ, and the Wong–Zakai term (v/2)∂Φ⟨(U·∇)U⟩_ρ cancel exactly on M, and the correlation adds ⟨∇ψ·K(A)U⟩_ρ = 0 for
every function K. A loop adapting in continuous time does not select among its exact fits through its measurement noise. Beyond the
hypothesis — a variance profile over the nodes, a noise correlated across them (a measurement offset; a real-time noise correlated on the
orbit's scale, τ_n ≳ T/N), a noise that reaches the adaptation through the loop and arrives correlated over the orbit — the node
covariance C weights the bilinear form below and its antisymmetry no longer removes the Stratonovich drift; on this gauge that drift is
O(γ) relative to its own Itô drift: in the slow-replicator limit the masses' part of ψ = ∂Φ·U vanishes to O(γ²) in a neighbourhood of
M — the masses' noise is the amplitudes' carried along the gauge —, a second mechanism, which several particles per class break
(Proposition D‴.42(iv)); the O(γ) law is asymptotic (γ ≲ 10⁻³ on the instance, γ ≲ 10⁻⁴ for the strongly modulated profile 1 + 0.8 sin t, whose O(γ) coefficient is small: the local exponent 1.4 between 10⁻³ and 10⁻⁴), and its constant grows like 1/a′ toward a saturation.

(iii) *(the selection per update)* With noise drawn afresh at each update of an Euler step h in z (the Itô interpretation: sampled-data
adaptation, label-noise gradient descent), the drift along M is −(v/2)∂Φ⟨(U·∇)U⟩_ρ up to O(hλ_max) ((iv) gives the whole factor). For a
Euclidean metric this is −(mv/4)∇_M tr ∇²J — label-noise SGD's flat-minimum selection. On the replicator's masses, in the slow-replicator
limit, it is the replicator flow of the fitness

    ū_k = −(v/2)β_kG_α⟨Φ_k²⟩_ρ(a′_k² − a_ka″_k) = −(v/2)β_kG_α⟨Φ_k²⟩_ρ(1 − q_k²) = −∂_{β_k}Ψ_ℓ,   q_k = (a_k/a_max)²,
    Ψ_ℓ(W) = (v/4)Σ_kG_α⟨Φ_k²⟩_ρ m²(W_k − W_min,k²/W_k)²

(the amplitudes' part of (mv/4)tr(G∇²J); the centres' and widths' parts are constant on M), strictly convex in W, with a unique minimiser
W_ℓ on the simplex, interior to the representable masses (W_ℓ,k > W_min,k for every k) — the slow limit's target. The Itô selection
depends on the coordinates of the update (the Stratonovich zero of (ii) does not): an Euler step in z′ = χ(z) adds −(v/2)∂Φ⟨∂²χ[U, U]⟩_ρ;
in the amplitude a itself instead of the network's parameter α the factor a′² − aa″ becomes a′² − 2aa″ = (1 − q)(1 + 3q), the fitness of
the strictly convex (v/2)Σ_kG_α⟨Φ_k²⟩_ρ(β_k²/2 + 2c_k log β_k + 3c_k²/(2β_k²)), c_k = (mA_k/a_max)², with an interior minimiser W_ℓᵃ.
Either fitness vanishes linearly at the saturation (q → 1), where the dither's diverges (Proposition D‴.37): fresh measurement noise draws
the masses away from the saturation, but does not hold them off it against a dither of comparable level.

(iv) *(correlated draws: the increment's second moment selects)* Let the draws be stationary, with step correlations ρ_d and per-step
variance σ_ξ² (homoscedastic and independent over the nodes), and the step h < 2/λ_max. At order v the Euler scheme's drift along M is
Katzenberger's drift of the filtered covariance

    Σ_f = Σ_{il} f_il Σ_il e_ie_lᵀ   (Σ_il the components of ⟨UUᵀ⟩_ρ in the eigenbasis (e_i, −λ_i) of A on the normal space),
    f_il = 1 − h(λ_iR(a_i) + λ_lR(a_l)) + h²λ_iλ_l(1 + G(a_i) + G(a_l))/(1 − a_ia_l),   a = 1 − hλ,  G(a) = Σ_{d≥1}ρ_da^d,  R(a) = G(a)/a,

times the per-update variance rate v_h := hσ_ξ²/N: the second moment of the whole increment h(F + ⟨Uξ⟩_ρ) — the normal deviation
responding to the past draws — over that of the noise. The intensity is v = v_hΣ_dρ_{|d|} ((1 + ρ)/(1 − ρ)·v_h for AR(1) noise
ρ_d = ρ^d). So: (a) if hλ_max ≪ 1 − ρ (λ_maxτ_c ≪ 1, τ_c the correlation time) f ≈ 1 and the selection is (1 − ρ)/(1 + ρ) times (iii)'s at
a fixed intensity — more for anti-correlated noise, 1/k of it for a draw kept k steps —; (b) for noise drawn afresh f_ii = 2/(2 − hλ_i),
and on a flat-metric gradient flow with label noise (Σ ∝ ∇²J on M) the selection descends tr Ψ(∇²J), Ψ′ = f_ii: here
Ψ(λ) = −(2/h)log(1 − hλ/2), Damian–Ma–Lee's finite-step regulariser, convex in λ (the stiff modes weigh more); (c) for an AR(1) noise —
a Markov noise, with white innovations — of correlation time τ_c sampled finely (h ≪ τ_c, 1/λ_max),
f_il → (1 + 2x_ix_l/(x_i + x_l))/((1 + x_i)(1 + x_l)), x = λτ_c (the active Ornstein–Uhlenbeck particle's filter 1/(1 + λτ_c) on the
diagonal), and Ψ(λ) → log(1 + λτ_c)/τ_c: the selected potential goes from the trace of the Hessian (τ_c → 0) to
(1/τ_c)log det(I + τ_c∇²J) — the log-determinant for a slow noise, which the stiff modes absorb (the residual follows the noise) —, so the
noise's colour reweights the normal modes and turns the selection's direction, not only its size. The log-determinant is the Markov
noise's: for any stationary noise sampled finely, of normalised spectral density ŝ, f(λ) = E[ṅ²]/σ_ξ² = ∫ŝ(ω)ω²/(λ² + ω²)dω/2π, the
response's velocity over the noise — decreasing in λ for every coloured noise, constant only for white noise —, so Ψ = ∫f is concave
for every colour, and tr Ψ(∇²J) is a concave function of the Hessian; a smooth noise (Gaussian step correlations, finite E[ξ̇²]) has
f ≈ (λτ_c)⁻² for λτ_c ≫ 1 and a bounded Ψ; (d) at a fixed physical noise the selection vanishes with h: (ii); Heun's scheme with the same draw in both stages integrates the ODE
driven by the draws' piecewise-constant path, and its O(v) selection is O((hλ)²) of the Euler scheme's, zero only as h → 0;
(e) *(a slow Markov measurement noise is a dither)* for label noise Σ = −m·AM on M, and an AR(1) noise with λ_minτ_c → ∞, the filter
turns it into τ_cΣ_f → X_h, X_h − BX_hBᵀ = 2hS (B = I + hA, S the normal part of Σ: the pair (i, l) weighted by 2/(λ_i + λ_l − hλ_iλ_l)),
and as h → 0 into −A_DΣQᵀ = m·QMQᵀ (A_D the group inverse, Q = I − P) — the flow's own mobility on the normal space, a thermal noise in the
flow's metric: the noise enters through the descent's fields (∝ A) and the slow filter divides by A —, so a slow Markov measurement noise
selects as a dither of the flow's mobility does: on the replicator's masses, in the slow-replicator limit, as Proposition D‴.37's dither of
temperature τ_eff = m·v_h/(2τ_c) — the entropic selection toward the saturation, the opposite of the fresh noise's interior target, which
Proposition D‴.38's correction at τ_eff cancels. Its size is small: τ_eff ≈ mvh/(4τ_c²) at a fixed intensity. The limit needs
λ_minτ_c ≫ 1, which fails near a saturation, where the softest normal rate vanishes. At a finite replicator rate the selection is
multistable instead: from τ_c ≈ 100 on three stable zeros, each with one class's mass large, and from τ_c = 10³ on an unstable node in
the middle, next to W♯ (Numerics (G)).

(v) *(with dither)* The leading-order drifts of independent noises add (Katzenberger's drift is linear in the covariance, the Wong–Zakai
terms of independent noises do not mix): with dither and measurement noise the masses' selection is the dither's (Proposition D‴.37) plus
(iii)'s, the latter zero in continuous time — so Proposition D‴.38's correction needs only the dither's level — and, by (iii), unable to
offset the dither's drive into the saturation near it.

(vi) *(two exact examples)* For the scalar factorisation f = uv fitted to y with label noise, the rescaling symmetry's charge
Q = u² − v² is conserved by the gradient flow and by the noise's field (v, u), hence pathwise by the Stratonovich dynamics, while an Euler
step multiplies it by exactly 1 − (ξ_n − r_n)²h² whatever the noise sequence: E[Q] decays at h·E[(ξ − r)²] per unit time — the per-step
variance times f(hλ), λ = u² + v² ((iv)); σ² for noise drawn afresh as h → 0, the Itô SDE's dQ = −σ²Q dt exactly. For the diagonal linear
network w = u⊙u − v⊙v fitted to n < d samples the products P_i = u_iv_i — the effective initialisation scales — are conserved likewise,
and an Euler step multiplies each by exactly 1 − 4h²(g_i − ξ̃_i)² (g = ∇_wL, ξ̃ = Xᵀξ/n): the selection — the descent of
tr ∇²L = (4/n)Σ_ic_i√(w_i² + 4P_i²) (c_i = Σ_jX_ji²), a weighted ℓ¹ norm Σ_ic_i|w_i| as P → 0 — runs at 4h²E[(X_iᵀe)²]/n² per step
(e = r − ξ), the per-step variance times Σ_jf(hκ_j)(X_iᵀq_j)²/c_i over the residual's modes (κ_j, q_j) of K = (4/n)X diag(u² + v²)Xᵀ: a
factor that differs from coordinate to coordinate when the noise is slow. Stratonovich noise does not move the interpolant. On a generic
overparametrised network the sharpness T = tr(JᵀJ)/n descends at −(v_h/4)∇T·P_T∇tr Ψ(K) (K = JᵀJ/n, P_T the orthogonal projection onto
the manifold's tangent), −(v/4)|P_T∇T|² for fresh noise at small h, not at all for Stratonovich noise (checked for ρ ≤ 0.9; slower noise
selects below the measurement's resolution there).

*Proof.* (i) ⟨U_x, t⟩_g = m(M∇f̂(x))ᵀM⁻¹t = m∇f̂(x)·t, and f̂ is constant along M. (ii) Φ is the limit map of F = ⟨rU⟩_ρ (r vanishes on
M), ψ_x = ∂Φ·U_x vanishes on M by (i), ∂Φ being the g-orthogonal projection onto TM there. The invariance ∂Φ·F ≡ 0 reads ⟨rψ⟩_ρ ≡ 0 near
M; differentiating twice at a point of M, where r and ψ vanish, gives ⟨∂_vr ∂_wψ + ∂_wr ∂_vψ⟩_ρ = 0: the bilinear form
B(v, w) := ⟨∂_vr ∂_wψ⟩_ρ is antisymmetric. In Stratonovich's form, Itô's formula gives dΦ(z) = ∂Φ·∘dz, whose drift at order v is
(v/2)⟨U·∇ψ⟩_ρ = −(mv/2)Σ_{ab}M_{ab}B(e_b, e_a) = −(mv/2)tr(MB) = 0, M symmetric, B antisymmetric; the same sum is Katzenberger's ½∂²Φ[Σ]
plus the Wong–Zakai term (v/2)∂Φ⟨(U·∇)U⟩_ρ (the product rule). For a smooth stationary noise of correlation R the linear response
δz(s) = ∫_0^∞e^{uA}⟨Uξ(s − u)⟩_ρ du gives the drift ⟨∇ψ·K(A)U⟩_ρ, K(A) = ∫_0^∞R(u)e^{uA}du, and on M, A = ⟨U∇rᵀ⟩_ρ = −M∇²J, so
⟨∇ψ·K(A)U⟩_ρ = −m tr(K(−M∇²J)M·B) = 0, K(−M∇²J)M = M K(−∇²JM) being symmetric. A node covariance C replaces B by
B_C(v, w) = N⁻²Σ_{xy}C_xy∂_vr_x∂_wψ_y, which the invariance does not make antisymmetric unless C ∝ I. The second mechanism: in the
slow-replicator limit ∂Φ reads the log-masses' component minus (γ/β_k)(a_k/(a′_kG_α)) times the amplitude's (the g-orthogonal projection
onto the gauge's tangent, δα_k = −(a_k/a′_k)δlog β_k), and the fields' two parts are proportional node by node — U^α_k = β_kG_αa′_kΦ_k,
U^{log β}_k = γ(a_kΦ_k − f̂) —, and the limit map reads them in that proportion at every point of the basin, not only on M: J depends
on β_k and α_k through β_ka_k (one particle per class), so u_k = −∂_{β_k}J = −g_k∂_{α_k}J with g_k = a_k/(β_ka′_k), and along the noiseless
flow at frozen masses u_k = g_kα̇_k/G_α — the masses' O(γ) displacement until the positions reach the exact fit is exactly
γΦ₁_k = (γ/G_α)(Γ_k(α_k*(β)) − Γ_k(α_k)), Γ′_k = g_k, α_k*(β) the exact fit's amplitude at the current masses. Hence
ψ^{log β}_{x,k} = U^{log β}_{x,k} + γ∂Φ₁_k·U_x + O(γ²) = γ(a_kΦ_k − f̂)(x) − (γ/G_α)g_kU^α_{x,k} + O(γ²) = −γf̂(x) + O(γ²) near M (∂α_k*(β)
enters through U^{log β} = O(γ)), the common part removed by Σβ = m; every C-weighted residual is carried by ∂ψ, so on the masses it is
O(γ²) against the Itô drift's O(γ). With several particles per class β_ka_k is no longer what J sees, and the residual stays
(Proposition D‴.42(iv)). (iii) The Itô drift is (ii)'s sum minus the Wong–Zakai term. On the

*Status.* (i) proved; (ii) proved at order v (given Katzenberger's theorem and, for white noise, the Wong–Zakai theorem; the smooth-noise
case by linear response), the residual's O(γ) relative order beyond the hypothesis proved at leading order in γ (one particle per
class; the asymptotic range numerical), its size numerical; (iii) proved
at leading order (the slow-replicator limit for the closed forms); (iv) proved at order v and at linear response, for any step h < 2/λ_max
and any stationary correlation (the O(hλ) terms included; Gaussian draws — the draws' third moments enter at O(v^{3/2})), (a)–(e)
corollaries ((c)'s concavity for any colour proved in the continuum limit; (e)'s finite-step limit proved, its identity with the
dither's direction proved in the slow-replicator limit away from the saturations and numerical at γ = 10⁻²; the zero set at finite γ
and τ_c numerical); (v) a corollary; (vi) the examples' identities exact per step,
their rates by (iv), the generic network's law at leading order. Classical: Katzenberger's theorem and its use for the noise-driven drift
along a manifold of minimisers (Li–Wang–Arora, [S64]); label-noise SGD's selection of flat minima — Blanc–Gupta–Valiant–Valiant,
Damian–Ma–Lee (with its finite-step regulariser −(1/2η)tr log(I − η∇²L/2)), Li–Wang–Arora, HaoChen–Wei–Lee–Ma, Shalova–Schlichting–
Peletier —, all with noise drawn independently at each step, the regulariser's scaling with step × variance among them; the Itô–Stratonovich
distinction, the Wong–Zakai theorem and noise-induced drifts (Wong–Zakai, van Kampen, Horsthemke–Lefever), and the crossover between
Itô's and Stratonovich's limits set by the ratio of the noise's correlation time to the relaxation time (Kupferman–Pavliotis–Stuart,
Pavliotis–Stuart); SDE models of SGD in Itô's form (Li–Tai–E, Li–Malladi–Arora); anti-correlated parameter noise as a regulariser of the
Hessian's trace (Orvieto et al.; perturbed gradients, a different mechanism), correlated parameter noise more generally (Lucchi–Proske–
Orvieto–Bach–Kersting), the anti-correlation of epoch-based minibatch noise, which lowers the weight variance along flat directions
(Kühn–Rosenow), SGD without replacement's weighted-trace regulariser with a Hessian-function weight (Beneventano), and a finite-learning-rate
Hessian-dependent regulariser of anti-correlated noise with a trade-off set by the correlation time (Kim et al., an abstract, flagged);
the continuum filter itself is the active Ornstein–Uhlenbeck particle's effective temperature T/(1 + kτ) in a trap of stiffness k, and
the factor det(I + τ∇²U) of the unified coloured-noise approximation's stationary law (Jung–Hänggi, Hänggi–Jung, Maggi et al.); the
isotropic noise's log-determinant drift along a manifold of minima (Li–Wang–Arora) is (e)'s target; the law of balance of rescaling symmetries under SGD (Ziyin–Li–Ueda) and
the noise equilibria of parameter symmetries (Ziyin–Wang–Li–Wu), of which (vi)'s Euler identities are exact discrete cases, the
Stratonovich conservation following from their Itô derivation; the diagonal network's label-noise Lasso (Pillaud-Vivien–Reygner–Flammarion,
in continuous time and Itô's reading) and its effective initialisation scale (Woodworth et al.) ([S69]). New (we did not find it stated):
the exact cancellation for noise entering through the error, for any temporal spectrum, by the antisymmetry the limit map's invariance
imposes — a loop adapting in continuous time does not select through its measurement noise —; for correlated draws the coloured filter of
label noise's drift along M — f_il, the cross term's mean vanishing by the same antisymmetry, Damian–Ma–Lee's regulariser its white case —
and its consequences: the passage from the trace to (1/τ_c)log det(I + τ_c∇²J) for a slow Markov noise, a concave selected potential for
every colour, a slow Markov measurement noise selecting as a dither of the flow's own mobility does; the closed forms on the replicator's
masses, with their dependence on the update's coordinates, and the selection's multistability on the gauge at finite rates.
